## Architecture and chronology

The initial Git root is 2025-05-14, not four years of this repository. GitHub's repository creation is 2026-02-04, while imported Git history predates it. The earliest implementation framework (May 2025, `321ef19cd5…`) had separate `apps/web` and `apps/workshop`, `packages/ui` using TSup, ESM+CJS and Tailwind 3, and CodeArtifact publishing. In 2025, components were built through successive primitives and React Aria migrations; Storybook/coverage work expanded in December. January 2026 (`3603b7b75beb…`) combined workshop stories and UI source into `packages/workshop-ui`. Old UI/workshop/web surfaces persisted temporarily and were removed in March (`8bd89ab56c…`, PR #30). This explains parallel fixes and duplicated historical patches; they are not separate product outcomes.

Current pnpm workspace globs are `apps/*` and `packages/*`, with Turbo dependency-ordered builds, shared TypeScript/config packages and public UI/AI/icons/MCP packages. UI and AI depend on shared tokens/icons and UI composition; the documentation app consumes the public packages. UI/AI are React 18 libraries, not applications with backend ownership. Current observed toolchain: pnpm 8.6.10; React 18.2; root TypeScript ~5.9.3; Vite 7.2.4; Storybook 10.1.11; Vitest 4.0.16; Tailwind 4.1.18; Docusaurus 3.10.1. ### LYRA-002 — Design tokens and theme cascade

Problem/context: consistent themes, light/dark modes, spacing/typography and alternate brands across reusable components. Contribution: token definitions, generation, mode/theme providers and palette expansion.

Flow: base JSON (colors, dimensions, radius, shadows, typography, borders) and semantic JSON enter `build-optimized-theme.js`. Style Dictionary custom transforms preserve underscore/kebab names, serialize compound shadows and convert px dimensions/font/line-height to rem. Original token references are deliberately preserved as CSS `var()` aliases rather than always baking resolved hex. Dark variants from `token.original.dark` become `light-dark(light,dark)`. `data-mode` sets inherited `color-scheme`; `data-theme` selects a brand palette. Shared semantic declarations are reapplied at each `[data-theme]`, because CSS custom-property aliases compute at the declaring element; a root-only alias would otherwise inherit a value fixed to the root brand. Themes build temporary CSS files, combine them and clean up intermediate files.

PR #132 adds 24 Material palettes (25–950 shades) to the existing default/neutral/responsive/plum/indigo themes, centralizes shared semantic tokens and preserves brand overrides. `ThemeProvider` writes body datasets and currently removes them on effect cleanup; `useTheme` provides local setters/toggle. `LyraScopedThemeProvider` uses a `.lyra` wrapper and an appended local portal container through `UNSAFE_PortalProvider`, with SSR document guard and removal on unmount, so Aria overlays stay inside the scoped token/CSS tree. Global body theming can interact with multiple providers; no independent concurrency guarantee is inferred.

Historical detail: PR #26/`848063c4e767…` describes “revert theme cleanup”; current inspected source **does contain cleanup**. Preserve the review/history and current code separately. Source references: `packages/design-tokens/tokens/{base,semantic}`, `build-optimized-theme.js`, UI `theme-provider/index.tsx`, PRs #1, #26, #77, #132. Validation: theme/provider/token tests, generated outputs and scoped-theme examples inspected. Status: released library/tooling; browser support for CSS `light-dark()` is a consumer constraint, not evidence of universal compatibility. Keywords/material: design tokens, Style Dictionary, theming, CSS cascade, scoped portals. Unknown: Figma token-export governance, customer theme adoption and measurable savings.

### LYRA-003 — CSS isolation, rem compatibility and animation preservation

Problem/context: embedding Lyra in applications with existing global CSS, different root font sizes and minifiers created integration conflicts. Contribution: prefixed/scoped style distribution, alternate rem build, keyframe namespace and targeted consumer/docs fixes.

Flow: Tailwind 4 `ly:` utilities and generated token CSS feed the library style build. PostCSS scripts create `.lyra`-scoped outputs, rewrite root/theme/mode selectors, avoid treating at-rules/keyframes as normal selectors, and handle component/utility importance separately from `@property`/font/keyframe rules. `build-rem-css.mjs` emits a 14px-root-compatible variant using 16/14 scaling and the tokens' separate `variables-14px.css` output; this is CSS integration compatibility, not runtime responsiveness. `build-scoped-css.mjs` and earlier `scope-base-layer.mjs` evolve base reset containment. Keyframe identifiers become `lyra-*`, and animation declarations/custom-property references are rewritten consistently to avoid name collisions.

Historical status: CSS-import-order hardening in PR #64/`6689fc0acc…` was reverted by `882d098bec32…` on April 1; do not describe that exact patch as current. PR #87 later scopes component selectors. PR #69 fixes Docusaurus's advanced CSS minifier removing/renaming keyframes without updating Lyra animation custom properties; the docs app forces the simple CSS minimizer. Its historical validation inspected the final loader selector/custom property/keyframe, proving a specific animation packaging fix rather than general performance improvement. PR #70 resolves base-unscoped layer conflicts.

### LYRA-004 — Buttons, grouped actions and reaction controls

Contribution: reusable button variants, icon/utility/grouped controls, loading/disabled behavior, copy/like/unlike interaction surfaces. React Aria press/focus semantics replaced early Radix button implementations (`e0187f4fe0…`, `2030b82a8a…`, August 2025); Slot/polymorphic cases remain distinct. CVA maps variants/sizes/icon placements to semantic tokens, while forwarded refs and consumers' event props preserve composition. Loading affects interactivity and visual state; PR #82 repairs disabled overrides during loading instead of merely displaying a spinner.

Button groups compose typed items and selected-state behavior; utility buttons provide constrained icon affordances. Reaction controls share `useReactionButtonState` and style constants, and CopyButton coordinates copy result/tooltip state; callback/clipboard error handling and tests are component-level behavior, not a platform-wide clipboard guarantee. Paths: UI `button`, `button-group`, `animated-icons`; their public exports, unit and Storybook tests. Sources: Aria migration commits, PRs #79/#82 and cleanup/test PRs. Status: current library; historical APIs/migrations in ledger. Validation covers rendering variants, disabled/loading interactions, state callbacks and tooltip/reaction branches. Keywords/material: component API design, React Aria, controlled actions, reusable state, regression fixes. Unknown: exact production button usage counts; no independently audited accessibility claim.

### LYRA-005 — Avatar, badge, tag and featured-icon surfaces

Contribution: configurable identity/status surfaces, Avatar groups/labels/profile-photo arrangements, Badge groups and Tag collections, token-based FeaturedIcon variants. Avatar uses Radix image/fallback primitives; statuses, size/density, icon/fallback and groups compose through typed interfaces. Badge's type-to-color map constrains valid combinations instead of accepting arbitrary strings; compound/nested exports preserve separate import boundaries. Tags represent selections and removable items, with consumer-driven callbacks; FeaturedIcon appearance/ring/outline maps retain design tokens.

Latest evolution: PR #151 (`ef704bbe8afc…` head; merge `7a55fd81f0f9…`) adds `chromatic` and `chromaticWeight` (`regular`/`bold`). Fallback initials are trimmed/uppercased, hashed deterministically into utility color families; regular/bold use 100/700 token surfaces. Digits/special characters stay in the hash; empty, icon or non-string fallbacks remain New Gray. Data attributes and CSS rules drive color styling. Loaded images preserve image behavior; group overflow `+N` remains gray. “Chromatic” here is an Avatar color mode, separate from the Chromatic visual testing service.

Paths/symbols: `avatar/chromatic.ts`, Avatar root/CSS, avatar-label/avatar-group, `badge`, `tag`, `featured-icon`; PR #151 description and regression tests. Status: Avatar change merged September 29 after the September 28 UI 3.2.0 release; registry publication/adoption of this specific change UNKNOWN. Earlier APIs are released library code. Tests verify normalized hash stability, fallback branches, image/group handling and token attributes. Keywords/material: deterministic UI, typed variants, identity components, backwards-compatible API extension. Unknown: real product deployment and whether the latest merged Avatar feature has since been published.

### LYRA-006 — Inputs, textarea, verification and payment formatting

Contribution: labeled/hinted/error input primitives, numeric/pattern behavior, adornments, textarea sizing/tags, OTP and payment-card formatting. Components compose Aria fields/validation with token variants and required `data-qa`; `Label`/`HintText` relationships and invalid/disabled state are implemented, not assumed from CSS. Input number behavior includes wheel/step handling; pattern/required/invalid paths are covered. PR #85 redesigns start/end adornments while retaining the deprecated `icon` compatibility path; trailing add-on is a separate surface, not an unverified synonym for endAdornment.

Textarea separates the base field from tag/auto-size composition, measures height and min rows and forwards change/ref behavior. VerificationCodeInput uses `input-otp`, validation/autofocus/invalid fixes and grouping; it does not implement SMS/email delivery or verification backend. PaymentInput formats card-number input and icon/type presentation; it is not payment authorization or PCI processing. Historical December/January test coverage and current unit/Storybook cases cover invalid formats, controlled changes, focus, adornments, character constraints and disabled branches.

### LYRA-008 — Static, searchable, asynchronous and grouped Select

Problem/context: a reusable selection API needed static options, editable search, incremental data, multi-select tags and grouped option UX. Contribution: compound `Select`, custom render props, async loading/state handling and subsequent fixes.

Static select and ComboBox use React Aria Components/Stately collections; multi-select receives selected item list data and manages tag/value presentation. `useSelectAsyncList` adapts a caller's `loadMore({signal,cursor,filterText})` to React Stately `useAsyncList`, preserving AbortSignal/cursor and using a ref for the latest loader. Loading, loading-more, error/empty and `aria-live` surfaces are explicit. Popover width tracks its trigger through measurement/ResizeObserver. Async behavior is a callback adapter, not an owned search backend.

Multi-select has selected-option filtering, custom option/tag renderers and max-visible-tag overflow/removal behavior. PRs #34/#36 add persistence/filterSelectedOptions choices; identical heads are not double-counted outcomes. Review #36 flags array typing and zero-visible-tag usability; do not assume every review suggestion was fixed without a corresponding revision. PR #71's searchable-select review was resolved by examining the installed React Aria versions: `value/onChange` represents selected key in the relevant ComboBox contract, while `inputValue/onInputChange` represents query text; deprecated key aliases differ by version. This is evidence of version-aware API debugging, not a blanket claim all Aria versions share one interface.

PR #140 closed without merge; #142 merged the later grouped-options implementation. An exclusive `items` versus `sections` TypeScript union plus development validation prevents mixed collection modes. Sections accept name/title/label and children/items, search labels/supporting text and remove empty groups. Container click focuses the input and opens the popover while remove-tag controls preserve their interaction; compound Section/Header exports and docs/tests were added. Metadata regeneration makes these props discoverable to MCP.

Paths/symbols: UI `select/index.tsx`, `multi-select.tsx`, shared types/helpers, `useSelectAsyncList`, selected-tag/option components and async tests. Primary PRs #34/#36/#71/#140/#142. Status: current/released grouped selection (UI 3.1.0 release evidence), closed precursor explicitly unmerged. Validation: controlled/static/async/filter/empty/error/group/container-focus and keyboard interaction tests. Keywords/material: asynchronous UI, abortable pagination, generic collection APIs, React Aria, state/data flow. Unknown: production data volumes, API response times or universal keyboard/WCAG certification.

### LYRA-010 — Overlay, modal, sheet, accordion and tooltip primitives

Contribution: reusable Modal/ModalBase composition (root/header/content/actions), Drawer positions, Popover/Tooltip triggers and placements, Vaul-backed Sheet and Aria-backed Accordion. Aria overlay/dialog primitives provide dismissal/focus semantics, while token classes, transition render props and consumer-controlled open state compose the visual/API boundary. Scroll locking is integrated through the upstream overlays patch, and scoped theme portals keep popovers within the theme tree (LYRA-002/035).

Tooltip/Dropdown bug fixes #90 and Modal aria-label fixes `29d374d076ab…` establish concrete accessibility-oriented maintenance. Different overlay primitives do not imply all surfaces share identical modal semantics.

### LYRA-011 — Compound Table, skeleton rows and pinned columns

Problem/context: consistent data-row display needed typed composition, selection/sorting, cell variants, loading skeletons and horizontal pinning. Contribution: `Table.Root`, table/head/header/body/row/cell APIs, context validation, cell renderers and later sticky-column features.

Flow: TableRoot normalizes selected keys from string arrays or `'all'` into Aria-compatible collections and converts selection callbacks back to the public shape, preserving select-all semantics. Root presence is set in the memoized context during the first render instead of a later effect, avoiding early child validation errors (PR #5). Children validate compound structure; contexts share column/cell settings. Cell renderers compose avatar/group, badge, text/icon, progress, rating, trend and actions with consumer data. Sorting/disabled keys/pagination remain explicit props/callbacks, not a backend query engine.

PR #86 adds skeleton loading rows, including automatic row-count/height behavior and deterministic manual control. The older reviewed revision `e749ceee7fdbb9c12efbf52d9c953e89a10742f8` was recovered from hosting: it adds `aria-busy` forwarding, skeleton rows/cells derived from visible registered columns, finite-positive count normalization, cyclic widths, screen-reader loading labels and a six-cell loading Storybook assertion. Its patch duplicates a locally available revision, so this is revision traceability rather than a second feature outcome. PR #146 adds `Table.Head pin='left'|'right'`, matching `columnId` on body cells. `table-column-pin` resolves widths (numeric width or minWidth), skips hidden pinned columns and accumulates offsets independently on each side, then applies sticky classes/styles to headers/cells. `bordered={false}` removes ring/row separators. Column pin tests and docs describe constraints for multiple pinned columns. Current working tree has additional uncommitted edits to these files; committed behavior was checked from HEAD, and those edits are separately labeled.

Sources: UI `table/{TableRoot,TableContext,TableHead,TableHeader,TableCellBase,table-column-pin}.tsx/ts`, renderer modules and tests; PRs #5/#86/#146; `d575af4de4…`; UI 3.2.0 release notes. Status: Table/pinning released library evidence; uncommitted follow-ups not included in that release claim. Keywords/material: generic table APIs, controlled selection, sticky layout, width/offset calculation, structural validation. Unknown: specific consumer datasets, benchmarked virtualization/performance and production adoption of individual variants. DataTable virtualization belongs to LYRA-037, not this committed Table API.

### LYRA-012 — Breadcrumb, pagination, Tabs and numeric Stepper

Contribution: tokenized breadcrumbs/current-item states, desktop/mobile pagination families, animated tabs and a numeric Stepper. Pagination utilities generate page windows/ellipsis, mobile page numbers, previous/next controls and formatted page text; component handlers enforce bounds and communicate chosen page. Card/minimal/dot/button-group variants share helpers instead of separate business pagination logic. Breadcrumb uses navigation/current-state labeling and hover/active token revisions (PR #76).

Tabs wrap Aria tab selection and responsive desktop/mobile renderers, calculate indicator dimensions/position and schedule its initial measurement. PR #81 introduces per-instance unique layout IDs so Motion indicators no longer animate across unrelated tab groups; it also updates initial-transition behavior. The older numeric Stepper controls increment/decrement values and bounds/key interactions; it is distinct from the later process ProgressStepper. Paths: `breadcrumb`, `pagination`, `tabs`, `stepper`, variant/util/helper modules; PR #81 and token/version follow-ups. ### LYRA-014 — Box, Flex, Grid, text, backgrounds and skeletons

Contribution: layout primitives and design surfaces with reusable style/state abstractions. Box supports a polymorphic `as` element, typed style/pseudo props and CSS conversion via a StyleSheetManager; numeric CSS property handling was fixed (`3eedb5bcce9c…`). Flex separates container/item props, parses responsive values in breakpoint order, resolves spacing/tokens, generates media queries, caches style hashes and warns about invalid container combinations. July PR #110 addresses Flex layout/size/wrap issues. Grid/GridItem add CSS-grid composition in January (`a5c3eddf6231…`). These are library layout abstractions, not a custom browser layout engine.

Text/Typography apply token typography and semantic element choices. Divider evolved to support an empty-content default as well as labeled separators (`f1b9fb53ee88…`). Background/decorative/overlay elements moved from DOM geometry to SVG and fixed square/dark-mode behavior in January. PR #71 review establishes that decorative backgrounds must not automatically gain `role='img'` solely because a string child exists; accessibility semantics depend on purpose. Skeleton context propagates loading state to wrappers/elements/text, while PrimitiveSkeleton handles standalone shapes/animation. Style/animation modules and reduced-motion branches are evidence of implementation, not an Apple-style design claim.

Paths: UI `box`, `flex`, `grid`, `divider`, `text`, `typography`, background families, `skeleton`, `primitive-skeleton`; relevant utilities/tests. Validation: numeric/style conversion, responsive ordering, class/prop behavior, loading contexts and shape/dark-mode regressions. Status: current library with removed DOM/background approaches historical. Keywords/material: polymorphic React, responsive styling, design-system primitives, CSS generation/caching, skeleton loading. Unknown: measured rendering gains and actual host screen counts.

### LYRA-016 — Recharts visualization components

Problem/context: reusable charts needed consistent token colors, legends, axes/tooltips and predictable edge-case behavior. Contribution: BarChart, LineChart, PieChart, RadarChart and ActivityGauge APIs plus Storybook/docs/tests. The base confirms bar/line/radar/activity-gauge work; Pie is additional code evidence, not an invented resume count.

Flow: caller record arrays and `ChartSeries` definitions drive Recharts marks through shared axis/grid/legend/tooltip helpers. Series colors map to CSS tokens, with supported custom colors. Tooltip formatting preserves categorical values rather than numerically coercing them; date labels use explicit date recognition. Tick spacing handles a one-item domain without division-by-zero. Bar stacking/rounding reflects stack position; Line gradients use unique IDs to avoid cross-instance collisions; Radar label/tick placement uses geometry and text measurement; ActivityGauge composes concentric activity values, labels/legends and truncation/tooltips. Consumer data/configuration determines values, not an owned analytics pipeline.

PR #13 review discussions and follow-ups address date/category handling, tick calculation, gauge label visibility, tooltip null values/numeric coercion, stacking defaults, dots and radar geometry. Later #41/#72/#83 fix chart edge cases and documentation examples. Reviewed dependency/import decisions matter because root barrels can pull optional Recharts dependencies; current package exports offer deep chart entries. Paths: UI `charts/{bar-chart,line-chart,pie-chart,radar-chart,activity-gauge,shared}`, generic types and tests; PR #13, #41, #72, #83. Status: component/tooling work, production analytics adoption UNKNOWN. Validation: formatter/domain/legend/empty data/geometry tests and visual stories, not a large-dataset benchmark. Keywords/material: Recharts, reusable visualization APIs, SVG, data formatting, edge-case debugging. Must not generalize to business reporting outcomes or measured large-scale analytics.

### LYRA-018 — Icon generation and modular distribution

Contribution: SVG-to-React generation, naming/export manifests, special icon categories, lazy loading and ESM package-size work. SVGR/generation scripts transform assets into typed React icons, normalize names and dimensions, generate barrel/loader/category entries and special file/payment/integration/video/TipTap surfaces. Figma REST download scripts are actual tooling with caller-provided authentication configuration; credential values are intentionally not retained. Generated assets/upstream icons preserve their provenance.

PR #126 replaces the large flattened runtime index with ESM modules and tiny re-export entry, stops publishing source, minifies, adds deep/category/special subpaths and removes oversized FolderAdvancedIcon. Generated icons accept `type` variants line/solid/duo-tone/duo-color, falling back to line if a style asset is absent; special icons use BaseIconProps to avoid incorrectly accepting generated style variants. Docs/Storybook galleries use lazy `icon-loaders`, avoiding eager `import *` of roughly 1,175 generated names.

Reported PR #126 measurements: npm pack about 6 MB → 1.10 MB (-81.7%); unpacked 14.30 → 6.70 MB (-53.1%); dist 9.50 → 6.41 MB (-32.5%); dist index 2.65 MB → 241 B. A three-icon fixture grew 1.73 → 4.75 KB because variants are retained. Preserve that tradeoff; icons do not satisfy a >90% claim for every artifact. Current check budget: pack ≤4 MiB and three-icon fixture ≤10 KiB with React external. Paths: `packages/icons/scripts/{generate-icons,build-package,check-bundle-size,measure-package-size,icon-generation-utils}`, assets/generated code, manifest and exports; PR #126. Status: released tooling/package; measurements historical reported validation. Keywords/material: package optimization, ESM, code generation, lazy imports, SVG pipelines. Unknown: independent current remeasurement and original asset-design ownership.

### LYRA-020 — Figma Code Connect mappings

Contribution: authored `.figma.tsx` mappings between Figma design nodes/properties and actual React APIs, with enum/boolean/string conversions, variant values, nested children and compound-component examples. July 2025 mappings began with Avatar (`96f27b0222…`); later mappings cover form controls, layout/overlays, charts, date pickers, Sheet and Activity Feed. The comprehensive guide documents the workflow and expected property mapping patterns.

Flow: `figma.connect` associates imported component, design node URL, props mapping and example JSX. These examples are implementation references, not a Figma rendering engine. The MCP server's `code-connect-examples.ts` parses these files with TypeScript AST, extracts component props/example variants/node references, normalizes paths and bundles metadata for portable usage without the full repository. Figma node URLs remain evidence pointers; external design contents were not accessible through configured connectors in this investigation.

Paths: component `figma/*.figma.tsx`, `FIGMA-CODE-CONNECT-GUIDE.md`, MCP `code-connect-examples.ts`; date picker PR/mapping revisions, #145 Activity Feed. Status: developer tooling; mapping source verified, publication/usage of every mapping UNKNOWN. Validation: examples/type mappings inspected, generated MCP examples cross-referenced; no new Figma publish command run. Keywords/material: design-to-code, Figma Code Connect, AST parsing, typed property translation. Do not claim measured implementation-time savings or universal automated fidelity.

### LYRA-021 — Lyra MCP server and component intelligence

Problem/context: agents needed reliable component discovery, props/tokens/docs and evidence-grounded design implementation instead of guessing APIs. Contribution: constructed the Node/TypeScript MCP server, CLI, schemas, tools/resources/prompts, source analysis and portable metadata. This is server development, not merely consuming MCP.

Transport/entry: `cli.ts` exposes `lyra-mcp` and `responsive-lyra-mcp`; no argument/serve starts an SDK server using `StdioServerTransport`. Current source has no HTTP deployment/authentication server or provider-backed model execution. TSup emits ESM CLI/library, and generation bundles docs/component/props/definitions/examples/tokens/pattern metadata with a manifest. Metadata is preferred (unless `LYRA_MCP_USE_METADATA=0`), cached by modification time; source analysis is fallback when metadata is missing. Thus published operation can work without a cloned design-system tree.

Discovery/data flow: `buildComponentIndex` uses TypeScript createProgram/checker, resolves exports/aliases and associates PascalCase runtime exports with prop-type symbols; UI takes precedence for duplicate names. `getComponentProps` uses checker.getProperties/typeToString/JSDoc/optional flags. Batch requests deduplicate names and return per-item NOT_FOUND errors without discarding successful results. Documentation and tokens are indexed from local/bundled sources; token lookup normalizes identifiers/CSS variables. AST extraction produces Code Connect examples. Source/index caching reduces repeated analysis. Known boundary: PascalCase heuristic may classify contexts/helpers as components, so its 142 index entries and 284 definition records are not the canonical component count; generated schemas also approximate TypeScript/React types and are not a compiler.

Registered tools (11): `get_workflow_requirements`, `resolve_and_compose_design`, `get_component_props`, `list_design_tokens`, `search_design_token`, `resolve_design_evidence`, `compose_design_implementation`, `search_components`, `audit_generated_implementation`, `get_component_definition`, `get_component_examples`. Zod schemas constrain array/chunk/limit/detail inputs; responses serialize structured JSON into MCP text content, with explicit validation/error handling. Static resources: `lyra://docs/consumer-guide`, `lyra://docs/workflow-contract`; dynamic component docs use `lyra://docs/component/{component}`. Prompts: `setup_lyra_consumer` and `figma_to_lyra_evidence_first`. CLI also lists patterns/docs/components. Tool descriptions/contracts, not a generic LLM chat agent, govern the workflow.

Design intelligence is deterministic: prioritize locked/exact Code Connect matches before lexical candidates; resolve design evidence into matched components/tokens/props; compose hierarchy/layout plans using Box/Flex/Grid and semantic `as`; preserve layout-critical paths and explicit unresolved items; audit supplied generated code for guessed APIs, raw layout markup, placeholders, missing matches and invented selected/chart data. Auditing is heuristic, not TypeScript execution, WCAG certification or an authenticated external API action. Ambiguity/clarification in these design plans is distinct from the external Google ADK platform.

History: closed #39 contains real server work and substantive reviews (enum parsing, required children, invalid examples, portable paths, mjs entry and context filtering); #48 merges the later MCP/docs initiative. `dfb647…`, `6787…`, `3935f598645b…` and later regeneration commits preserve revisions, while latest manifests/releases establish current server packaging. Paths: `packages/lyra-mcp/src/{mcp-server,component-index,component-props,component-intelligence,code-connect-examples,design-tokens,metadata-store,resource-catalog,generate-metadata,cli}`, metadata and README. Validation: source/schema/generated metadata and PR revisions inspected; no server/tools run against user systems here. Status: released developer tooling (MCP 2.1.0 release evidence). Keywords/material: MCP server construction, Zod, TypeScript AST/checker, schemas, stdio transport, resources/prompts, deterministic retrieval/validation. Unknown: enterprise distribution/user counts, productivity metric, external deployment and provider/auth integration beyond caller usage.

### LYRA-022 — Package publishing, registry migration and releases

<!-- REVERIFY-20261003:START -->
**LATEST USER CONFIRMATION — 2026-10-03:** Approved default public BASE wording: Reduced published design-system package sizes by over 90% across nearly all packages using modular ESM builds. Detailed UI/AI artifact measurements and differing icon results below remain preserved; do not convert package reduction into page-load/runtime gain or invent per-package numbers. This supersedes earlier contradictory attribution for current resume/application use; retained historical text follows.
<!-- REVERIFY-20261003:END -->

Contribution: authored library build/export/declaration boundaries, published packages, size budgets, registry migration and release automation. Early `@lyra/ui` used ESM+CJS; current UI/AI Vite/Rollup builds are **ESM-only**, minified, without source maps, with `preserveModules`/`preserveModulesRoot=src`. Public component entries are derived from the barrel, and export maps remap component paths, styles, hooks/utils and nested surfaces. Bare/node_modules imports stay external; source aliases remain internal. Declaration builds exclude stories/tests/Figma/style-only entries. CSS is imported explicitly and listed as side effects; empty style JS stubs are removed. AI markdown CSS is a separate style entry to avoid duplicating the full UI/token/font surface. Heavy optional peers are installed only when consumers use the relevant surface; a root import can still traverse broad re-exports, so deep imports are the defensible usage recommendation.

PR #127 reported npm-pack UI 6.1 MB →463 KB (-92.4%), AI 4.0 MB →148 KB (-96.3%); unpacked UI 30.8→2.60 MB (-91.6%), AI 13.4→617 KB (-95.5%). These verify the concrete UI/AI artifact reductions. The user confirms Lyra AI/UI as the relevant package scope, resolving the earlier question; PR #127 is the inspected supporting PR. Preserve the approved F/S wording “over 90% across nearly all packages” with this published-artifact scope. Icons have different verified reductions and no equivalent MCP reduction is asserted. These measurements do not establish page-load speed. The same PR reports local consumer installation-tree estimates (prod+dev dependencies → usage-based optional peers): app_v2 478→418 MB (12.6%), pursuit 269→214 MB (20.4%), responsive-lite 461→425 MB (7.8%), ask 298→262 MB (12.1%). Its lockfile was not rewritten; treat these as PR-reported local estimates, not verified deployed application footprint or a new benchmark.

Size-check flow: npm pack dry-run output plus esbuild consumer fixtures (React/heavy peers external) are compared to limits; CSS selectors/import declarations are checked separately. UI budget pack 1 MiB, Button fixture 80 KiB, chart wrapper 80 KiB with Recharts external; AI pack 400 KiB, PromptInput 120 KiB, AIResponse 80 KiB with Streamdown external. These wrapper fixture sizes exclude external engines and are not whole-app bundle sizes. Icons have LYRA-018's budgets.

Registry evolution: CodeArtifact (early 2025) → JFrog Artifactory (historical setup) → GitHub Packages September 2026 (`@responsive-lyra/*`, PR #133). Changesets generate version/changelog PRs, then publish on base-branch push; manifests and current scope/version reflect that migration. Temporary Vite/TypeScript/Docusaurus dual-scope aliases let repository tooling resolve old/new names during transition; they do not make every external consumer's old imports universally compatible. `repack-and-upload-backup.mjs` rewrites package metadata/imports from historical artifacts and can dry-run/repack/upload with bounded processing; PR #133 checks off both dry-run and publish-all for 66 historical versions. Preserve that reported execution, while complete registry backfill cannot independently be confirmed because read:packages is unavailable.

Other packaging details: published fallback strings were reduced to English while Storybook/docs register extra preview languages locally; Google Fonts import moved out of UI CSS, leaving font loading/`--font-family-body` to the consuming app. AI markdown CSS uses `@reference` to avoid resetting UI font variables. TableCellBase was split to break preserveModules cycles through cell renderers. These are observed compatibility/size decisions, not invented business rationale.

Operational evidence: the first September 8 release job failed at Changesets with GitHub organization SAML enforcement; later jobs successfully publish the named packages. Three inspected logs explicitly list published packages (runs 34195730914,34218170691,36380545987). The September 29 Avatar merge run 36569757121 reports no changesets and does not list a new publication, so latest Avatar is confirmed merged but not included in the last observed release. No credential values are retained.

Sources: UI/AI vite configs, export maps, declaration configs, `scripts/assert-declared-package-imports.mjs`, `drop-empty-style-mjs.mjs`, check/measure scripts, `.changeset`, release workflow and repack script; PR #127/#133/#134/#135/#143/#149/#150. Eleven GitHub release records support released UI/AI/icons/MCP versions; successful workflow runs do not alone prove every run published packages. ### LYRA-023 — Build orchestration, CI and cache seeding

Contribution: Turbo task graph, package/build separation, GitHub verification/release workflows, shared caches and bounded build file operations. Current merge pipeline runs on PR opened/synchronize/reopened into staging/master (or dispatch), Node 22 on ubuntu-latest, frozen pnpm install, build, UI/AI/icon size checks, strict lint and typecheck, with a 20-minute timeout. Superseded PR runs cancel; titles starting `[skip ci]` skip verification. Current merge workflow does not run the entire Vitest/Chromatic/Sonar suite; keep those workflows' evidence separate.

Historical Bitbucket CI was also implemented: `4486dca…` adds a Node 22 bullseye pipeline for pull-request linting against the UI dependency graph with pnpm/Corepack and initially frozen installation; `ed2b4be…` changes the install mode to no-frozen-lockfile. `d319b56…` renames the singular pipeline filename to `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`; January `106a13f…` changes the filter to the then-active UI-v2 surface. The file persisted through migration, drew an unresolved cleanup review in GitHub PR #44, and was deleted in September by `94690ce…` / PR #139. Its actual configuration is historical tooling evidence; it does not establish Jenkins or a current Bitbucket pipeline execution result. Full SHAs and file diffs are preserved in the commit ledger.

PR #109 build work reduces CI artifact pressure: Storybook Vite disables CI source maps and Rollup `maxParallelFileOps` is 2; package builds avoid rebuilding Storybook; coverage HTML is omitted in CI through a reporter selector. These address heavy build/disk use and ENOSPC conditions. `is-ci.ts` recognizes CI/JENKINS_URL/BUILD_NUMBER, which demonstrates environment-aware build behavior but not a Jenkinsfile implementation. This repo is primarily Vite/Rollup; Docusaurus uses its own build stack. The approved 101.45-second Webpack full-monorepo benchmark belongs to **rfp-app**, as USER-CONFIRMED in LYRA-038; it is separate from this repository’s Vite/build/test measurements.

PR #122 explains a concrete cache defect: caches created on sibling PR merge refs cannot be restored by another PR; the default/base branch is visible. The implementation splits validation from `cache-seed.yml`, which runs on pushes to staging/master and builds after dependency installation. Matching pnpm-lock hash and Turbo commit keys plus restore-key fallbacks allow subsequent PRs to restore base-branch artifacts. Per-branch seed runs serialize and do not cancel mid-save; verification cancels superseded PR runs. Both cache scopes and invalidation inputs matter; no unsupported new cold-build improvement percentage is inferred from this logic. Required-check ruleset JSON documents the expected merge status.

Sources: `turbo.json`, `.github/workflows/{merge-pipeline,cache-seed,release}.yml`, `.github/rulesets`, `.storybook/main.ts`, scripts/is-ci and coverage reporters; PRs #46/#47/#109/#118–#123. Closed cache experiments #118/#119/#120 and merged #121 precede #122; not all experiment branches were released. Validation: historical build/type/lint CI references, configurations and reported failure handling inspected. Status: current developer tooling. Keywords/material: CI caches, bounded concurrency, build orchestration, artifact pressure, GitHub Actions, frozen dependencies. ### LYRA-024 — Vitest, Storybook, accessibility and visual testing

Contribution: extensive component unit/coverage tests, browser-backed interaction stories, accessibility addon and visual tooling, then test-architecture optimization. Early scaffold had a no-tests placeholder; December 2025 onward adds meaningful component suites and coverage, January colocation preserves them, later revamps move behavior to unit tests and keep focused Storybook integration cases. A skill file alone is not implementation evidence: actual tests/configuration and historical diffs are the basis here.

Current root Vitest projects: `ui-unit`/`ai-unit` use jsdom and React setup; `icons-unit`/`scripts-unit` use Node; Storybook uses addon-vitest with Playwright headless Chromium and project annotations. Browser coverage is disabled; V8 unit coverage includes UI components/hooks/utils and AI components/lib. Stories, tests, Figma, icons/Typography and canvas testing helpers are excluded. Reporters emit LCOV/text/json, with HTML omitted in CI; `reportOnFailure` means LCOV can exist even when tests fail. No independent WCAG audit or universal numerical coverage threshold was established.

PR #131 splits the default unit command from the import-heavy browser project, restricts Tailwind to browser tests, routes AI tests to UI deep imports instead of the root barrel, avoids transforming ~1,175 icon source modules by resolving built icons/mocks, memoizes resolver/stat work, bounds thread workers (current 8), and keeps file parallelism/isolation. Shared lean jest-dom setup and targeted TipTap shims avoid global test overhead; i18n order/shuffle fixes reduce cross-test state. Reported wall clock: 173.62→75.93s unit command (-56.3%); coverage 194.64→85.01s (-56.3%); separate warm Storybook suite 58.23s with 107 files/223 tests; changed-file loop 1.5–5.1s. The PR states a **10-core host and 3 consecutive runs per workflow**; OS/CPU model/cache details remain unspecified. Reported unit suite 188 files/2,989 tests plus browser 223 =3,212 passed, with scoped coverage 99.97% statements/96.84% branches/100% functions. These are historical PR measurements, not fresh current totals, and the baseline/default workflow scope changed.

Additional historical diagnostics in that PR: transform 125.24→12.94s(-89.7%), aggregate worker module-import time 1,140.77→311.75s(-72.7%,829.02 worker seconds saved), setup 123.13→57.12s(-53.6%). Aggregate worker timings must not be added to wall-clock duration or recast as application runtime. The PR reports shuffle-order validation and unchanged coverage scope; source exclusions above limit generalization.

Meaningful cases span controlled/uncontrolled callbacks, Select abort/cursor/error/sections, Table root/selection/pin widths, timezone/date conversion and Apply/Cancel, dropdown keyboard/trigger semantics, Tabs instance IDs, chart category/date/one-tick handling, voice/transcript state, upload rejection/partial failures and Canvas snapshots/diff acceptance/stale sessions. Storybook uses `data-qa` consistently and actual `play` functions with user interactions/assertions. Thus automated accessibility evidence must not become a full contrast/WCAG audit claim.

### LYRA-026 — Localization and locale integration

Problem/context: library-owned strings needed caller app localization, preview fallbacks and React Aria locale alignment without binding the library to one host app. Contribution: translation hooks/resources, i18next runtime adapters/loaders, locale-aware providers and component string replacement.

Flow: `useLyraTranslation` chooses caller React I18nContext, configured Lyra app instance, then fallback instance for Aria locale; `useTranslation` is called with Suspense disabled and a typed string-returning wrapper. `createLyraI18n` normalizes configuration and creates/reuses caller-compatible runtime; dynamic namespace bundles merge actions/labels/message/tooltip maps. Optional `translateGet` adapts a consumer-supplied axiosGet to `/translate/get`, passing appVersion/lang and policy-driven podName. Errors go to supplied logger and return undefined; backend request wrapper supplies 200/500 callback status and optional legacy JSON payload behavior. No auth token is created here: authentication belongs to the supplied request client.

Plugin WeakSets avoid duplicate registration unless legacy re-registration is explicitly requested. Init signatures/promise tracking avoid redundant app initialization; reset/podName and isolated preview-instance APIs support existing host integration. `resolve-i18next-runtime.ts` handles ESM/default/runtime API shapes. Locale normalization and React Aria locale mapping reconcile language resources with date/keyboard formatting. Static fallback resources, preview registration, LyraWrapper and docs/Storybook locale toolbar keep demos usable when no app i18n exists. PR #68 is a closed draft; later actual code (#93/#113 and follow-ups) demonstrates integration rather than treating that draft as released.

Paths: UI `src/i18n/*`, `components/hooks/use-lyra-translation.ts`, `lyra-wrapper`, previews; PR #113 and localization tests. Status: current library/tooling; draft precursor historical/unmerged. Validation: runtime-shape tests, provider precedence, initialization/reset, fallback and locale tests. Keywords/material: internationalization, i18next, dependency/runtime interoperability, asynchronous loaders, compatibility adapters. Unknown: translated language quality, deployment markets and host-auth mechanism; translation request execution does not establish the external AI integration backend.

Source comes from official/third-party ShadCN registries using `aria-vega`; retained README explicitly labels vendored code inherited rather than authored. The engineering contribution is bridge/configuration/import/prefix integration and evaluation, not original invention of upstream components.

Flow: `components.json` configures React Aria base, aliases and `ly:` prefix. `shadcn-bridge.css` maps background/foreground/card/popover/primary/secondary/muted/accent/destructive/border/input/ring/chart/sidebar vocabularies to Lyra semantic variables. Tokens are redeclared under root and each data-theme, `@theme inline` avoids root-fixed aliases, and custom dark variant targets `data-mode='dark'`. Existing Lyra geometry/radii remain compatible. Vendor-prefix checking catches unreliable external registry prefixes. “shadcn apply” was explicitly avoided because it would overwrite Lyra globals with upstream OKLCH/fonts/.dark assumptions. Files stayed private unless deliberately exported.

### LYRA-028 — AI responses, chat, trace presentation and feedback

Contribution: AIResponse/ResponseBlock, chat-message/status, ChainOfThoughts, ShimmerText and FeedbackModal interface families, separate from a model/backend platform. AIResponse accepts caller markdown/actions/rating/sources/trace analysis; callback wiring and controlled/internal presentation manage retry/copy/feedback and disclosures. Source URL/hostname/favicon helpers derive display references. Trace scores and step states are supplied data, not calibrated confidence/reasoning computed by this library.

ResponseBlock renders a plain whitespace-preserving fallback during SSR/initial load, then dynamically imports cached ResponseBlockClient. A module-level promise/component cache avoids repeated imports and a mounted guard prevents state updates after unmount. Streamdown handles incremental markdown with CJK/code/math plugins, customized token-based heading/paragraph/image/blockquote renderers and accessible task-checkbox names. The current implementation sets `linkSafety.enabled=false`; this is an observed renderer setting, not evidence of a comprehensive responsible-AI/content-security policy. Import rejection handling is not claimed beyond the observed promise/mounted guard. `isAnimating` is a rendering prop, not an SSE transport.

ChainOfThoughts renders caller-provided step status, summary/media/source and collapsible content; it does not inspect private model reasoning or implement agent tracing. AIChatMessage distinguishes chat status/content, and shimmer signals work in progress. FeedbackModal collects reason/text through caller submission, not an analytics service. PR #92 closed; #93 merges the AI package initiative; #97 and follow-ups fix rendering/API issues, SSR/dependency compatibility and stories. Paths: AI families, ResponseBlock/Client, action/source/trace helpers, source-utils and CSS. Status: released AI UI package; exact product/LLM/provider adoption UNKNOWN. ### LYRA-029 — Clarification Questions controller

Problem/context: collect multi-turn structured user input for a caller-owned AI workflow. Contribution: a typed question/answer protocol and reusable controller/renderers, initially Input Request form then ClarificationQuestions.

Flow: discriminated questions/answers cover single-select, multi-select with optional free text, reorder and file. IDs key persistent answer/skip state; supplied answers restore partially filled flows. Single-select auto-advances/submits; multi-select requires explicit Next/Submit, required questions suppress Skip/Escape, reorder's original order is a valid answer. Helpers derive answered state and primary actions; controller/state/handler hooks coordinate forward/backward transitions, header/footer/keyboard behavior and callback payloads. `onChange` returns the active question answer/skip state; `onSubmit` emits all resolved questions plus formatted Q/A consolidated text; `onClose` returns current state. This prepares structured prompt context but does not route ADK tools or invoke GPT itself.

File questions require `uploadFile(File): Promise<UploadedFile>`. Selected files get stable name/size/lastModified placeholders, then Promise.allSettled uploads allow partial success. Fulfilled descriptors become completed/100% with preserved ID; rejection becomes per-file error text. Only completed files count as answered; UI max-size/count/accept/removal and busy states compose the shared upload component. There is no guarantee of backend retry/cancellation beyond implemented callbacks.

Evolution: #94–#102 and related commits build/refine question forms; #130 decomposes state/controller/handlers and expands tests. Current source/defaults matter more than doc comments (e.g. file renderer uses `multiple ?? true` while a type comment states false), so a future implementation answer must inspect the current contract rather than quote a default blindly. Paths: AI `clarification-questions/{types,ClarificationQuestions,useClarificationQuestionsController,useClarificationQuestionsState,useClarificationHandlers,format-answer,questions/*}`. Status: current released UI; external platform deployment UNKNOWN. Validation: question/answer narrowing, required/skip/back navigation, initial answers, keyboard reorder, file rejection/partial success and consolidated payload tests. Keywords/material: discriminated unions, state machines, asynchronous partial failure, multi-step forms, human clarification. No automation accuracy or user-completion metric established.

### LYRA-030 — Prompt Input, mentions, attachments and voice

Contribution: controlled/internal prompt composition with submit/stop callbacks, starters/tags, mention autocomplete, drag/drop attachments and browser speech input. Public ref exposes focus/clear/read prompt/files. Caller prompt changes flow through state and `onPromptChange`; submit passes text/files; `isWorking` selects Stop behavior. Splitting field/actions/overlays/tags/file modal and keyboard helpers in #130 preserves APIs while reducing component complexity.

Mentions parse cursor-local tokens, measure text/caret coordinates for an anchored dropdown, track active agent/user options and highlighted items, and handle Arrow/Enter/Escape selection. Tags/agent popovers are caller data, not a registry search backend. Drop overlay listens to window drag/drop; `matchesAccept` supports extension, exact MIME and wildcard MIME. Validation respects max bytes/count/current attachments/multiple and returns accepted versus type/size rejection lists; overflow files are not silently claimed as uploaded. Notifications display rejection information and files can be removed.

Voice hook detects SpeechRecognition/webkitSpeechRecognition (none on SSR/unsupported browser), configures continuous/interim results, combines the complete session transcript with the original prompt and guards cancelled sessions. Cancel stops listening and restores the original text; start exceptions reset local listening state; cleanup removes listeners/stops recognition. Current end/error event handlers are empty, so do not claim automatic reset/retry on every recognition error. Speech activity holds waveform animation briefly; audio analyser/media-stream hook handles microphone visualization and lifecycle cleanup. This is browser speech capability, not an owned transcription model or universal browser support.

Paths: AI `prompt-input/{PromptInput,core,mentions,file-drop,hooks,voice,notifications}`, #103/#104/#106/#112/#123/#130. Status: current released UI; exact external model/backend connections UNKNOWN. Validation: prompt/ref/keyboard, mention parsing, MIME/size/count rejection, drop handling, speech/cancel/listener tests and stories. Keywords/material: AI UX, controlled input, autocomplete, browser speech APIs, file validation, event cleanup. No measured input latency or universal speech-recognition compatibility.

### LYRA-031 — Canvas editor and AI rewrite sessions

Problem/context: rich content editing needed model-assisted selection rewrites with review/accept/discard semantics while preserving document structure. Contribution: TipTap-based Canvas extensions, toolbar/menu surfaces and a custom rewrite-session layer; upstream TipTap/ProseMirror and imported UI patterns retain provenance.

Editor surface: paragraphs/headings/lists/code highlighting, images, tables/links/emoji/math, slash commands, drag handles, selection/floating toolbar, heading minimap and content conversion. Markdown/HTML input handling normalizes content and suppresses redundant synchronization; inline double-dollar math migrates to math nodes outside code blocks. Content callbacks serialize current format; they are suppressed during an active AI operation to avoid propagating transient insertion/deletion markup as ordinary external edits.

Rewrite flow: a suggestion/custom prompt plus selection captures `from/to`, selected text, primary node ID and original block JSON snapshots. `rewriteCallback(suggestionId,nodeId,selectedText,prompt)` delegates the actual model request to the consumer; it returns void, and an absent handler shows an unavailable toast. The consumer delivers the result through the separate `rewritedContent` prop, whose `{id,content}` is copied to internal state. Session state stores originals/prompt, disables editing and starts a 60,000ms thinking timeout. The result ID must match the original node; refs/session tokens prevent an older typing animation from editing a newer/destroyed session. Word diff creates added/removed/unchanged typing steps, batches them and inserts text using insertion/deletion marks on a timer (15ms source constant). Completion stores a mapped change range, re-enables editing and offers review actions. The result contract identifies a node rather than a backend request ID, so do not generalize these animation guards into a guarantee against every out-of-order response for the same node.

Accept finds deletion-marked leaf spans, deletes them back-to-front, maps the range through the transaction, removes insertion marks and focuses the resulting selection. Discard restores captured block snapshots (fallback original node JSON); Try Again restores originals before invoking the same consumer callback/prompt. Cleanup cancels timers and clears thinking state; session guards address animation cancellation and destroyed editors. These mechanisms are stronger evidence than a generic “AI editor” description, but they do not prove server auth, model safety or perfect semantic diff preservation.

History: #105 introduces Canvas; review requests separation of concerns, with an explicit incremental-refactor response. #128/#129 unmerged precursors and #130 implement focused session/state/effect/action/content/extensions modules, utilities and tests. Paths: AI `canvas/editor`, `canvas/lib/{ai-session,diff-words,content-type,markdown-content}`, extensions, toolbars and minimap. Status: current released component package; production editor/backend usage UNKNOWN. Validation: snapshots/restoration, rewrite prompt/no-handler, accept/discard/retry, stale token/editor destruction, diff/batching/content sync, image/table/menu and callback tests. Keywords/material: TipTap, ProseMirror transactions, rich-text editing, state machines, asynchronous race handling, human review of edits. Do not claim model-provider implementation, SSE transport or an enterprise responsible-AI policy from this UI.

### LYRA-034 — Oxlint/Oxfmt quality workflow migration

Contribution: September PR #144 replaces ESLint/Prettier with Oxlint/Oxfmt, ports applicable rules/configuration and custom Lyra barrel-import guard, updates package scripts and formats source. `run-quality.mjs` coordinates quality commands; TypeScript checking stays separately explicit. Generated icon/style/vendor exclusions and package scopes matter to measured workload. The AST/plugin guard discourages broad barrels where deep imports avoid dependency/transform costs, and its tests exercise the rule.

Reported measurements: Prettier check 10.8s → Oxfmt check 1.3s (2,544 files); lint 23.6s → Oxlint 1.45s; separate tsc 5.9s→6.7s; sequential total around 40s→9.5s (~4×). Baseline lint included tsc and the chosen “1A” migration dropped ESLint type-aware unsafe/misused-promises checks; separate tsc does not replace every such lint rule. Preserve this scope/tradeoff rather than claiming a perfectly identical 16× lint workload or adding these to cold-build/runtime results.

### LYRA-039 — Calendar, date picker and timezone adapters

Contribution: Calendar/RangeCalendar/DateInput, desktop popovers/mobile modal date pickers, presets and compatibility adapters for caller Date/dayjs-like/string/timestamp values. Initial January `9f48af64723b…` implementation and subsequent responsive/timezone/state refactors preserve a substantial capability absent from the original resume topics. PR #15 labels the first release Beta; current interfaces exist, but an independently declared graduation from Beta was not located.

Flow: adapters recognize @internationalized/date values, JS Date/timestamps, ISO/date-only strings and dayjs/moment-like methods, convert to CalendarDate and apply timezone-aware Intl formatting to Date/timestamps. Provider defaults to browser zone or UTC on server. Outbound selected values are formatted local wall-clock strings `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` **without offset**, not guaranteed UTC instants. Invalid/unrecognized inputs return null in supported branches; no blanket exception guarantee for invalid timezone/constructor inputs is inferred. Range adapters accept array or `{start,end}`. Date-only conversion avoids accidentally shifting the selected calendar day through UTC serialization.

Controlled/uncontrolled committed value is separate from draftValue while the picker is open. Open initializes the draft; default Apply commits and invokes onApply; Cancel restores committed state/invokes onCancel; `shouldCloseOnSelect` commits immediately. Desktop uses Aria Popover, mobile below 768px ModalOverlay/Dialog; custom trigger/dialog/overlay classes are exposed. Closing schedules trigger blur via requestAnimationFrame and cleans up that request. Presets compute today/week/month/year/all-time from zone and locale; range focus/highlights and min/max constraints compose the Aria calendar. `3abdb9dafaf9…` fixes preserving locale-dependent week start instead of assuming Monday.

Paths: UI `date-picker/{date-adapters,date-picker,date-range-picker,shared,calendar,range-calendar,calendar-grid,date-input,cell,range-preset}`, `timezone-provider`; January revisions, PR #71 review/follow-up and tests/docs/Figma. Status: current library; historical first release Beta. Validation: conversions/zone/fallback/ranges, Apply/Cancel/controlled values, mobile/desktop and locale/week-start tests. Keywords/material: date/timezone handling, compatibility adapters, staged form state, responsive accessible popovers, localization. Unknown: all timezone/DST deployment cases and product adoption.

### LYRA-041 — Controlled state, refs and shared utilities

Contribution: shared hook/type/ref/utility contracts supporting component consistency. `useControlledState` treats undefined as uncontrolled and null as a controlled cleared value, initializes from supplied/default state, uses Object.is to avoid duplicate callbacks and warns in development when switching control mode. Uncontrolled updates track the current value within the setter so consecutive batched calls behave consistently; function-updater handling is implemented with a development warning. This resembles an upstream Spectrum pattern and preserves that provenance rather than claiming independent invention of the pattern.

Ref utilities expose DOM/focusable interfaces and imperative focus/root access while adapting forward refs. `cn` combines clsx/Tailwind merge; QA/default ID utilities and React-component type guards centralize shared behavior. File-type extension/icon utilities map categories to special icons with fallback; AI source helpers parse URL/hostname/favicon candidates with guarded invalid URL handling. Component resize/breakpoint/list hooks adapt observer/media/Aria state and cleanup lifecycles.

Paths: UI `src/hooks/{useControlledState,useDOMRef,refs,index}`, `src/utils`, component hooks; AI `src/lib/source-utils`; December shared-utility tests and later refactors. Status: current foundational library code. Validation: null/undefined control distinctions, callback equality/batching, ref focus/cleanup, filename/URL and class/type-guard tests. Keywords/material: reusable hooks, controlled/uncontrolled APIs, refs, utility abstraction, React lifecycle. Unknown: measured code-size/runtime improvement attributable solely to these helpers.
